To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully prepared PEGylated ORI conjugates and the pharmacokinetics and antitumor activities of the conjugates were improved.

the PEGylated conjugates with different molecular weights showed different release features and the drug solubilization and release features of PEGylate conjugates were relevant with molecular weight of PEG.
the PEG-SA-ORI polymeric conjugates were synthesized, and the in vitro release and in vivo pharmacokinetics of ORI were improved by PEGylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, in vivo pharmacokinetic and in vitro release studies of a series of novel PEGylated ORI conjugates.
the synthesis, in vitro and pharmacokinetic studies of PEG-SA-ORI, which may provide a new strategy to solve the solubility and plasma clearance problems of ORI.
the preparation, characterization and in vitro and in vitro evaluation of PEG-SA-ORI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PEGylation is a feasible method to improve the solubility, pharmacokinetics and in vivo efficacy of ORI.
PEGylation is an attractive approach to improve the pharmacokinetic properties of ORI, and the PEG-SA-ORI with MW of 5000 Da was the best choice for the in vivo application.
the PEGylation technology could improve the drug solubilization and release, and prolong the plasma circulation half-life of oridonin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conjugate of PEG-SA-ORI with lower MW PEG (MW = 5 kD) showed a more favorable pharmacokinetic behavior and a better in vivo antitumor effect in comparison with other conjugates.
PEGylated ORI conjugates could be used to improve the solubility of ORI, prolong its plasma half-life and sustain its release, which might be beneficial to its antitumor efficacy.
the PEGylation technology could improve the aqueous solubilities, release features, pharmacokinetic profiles, and antitumor efficacy of ORI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEGylated ORI could be a promising drug delivery system for the treatment of leukemia.

PEGylation could improve the solubility of ORI and its pharmacokinetic properties in vivo, and PEGylation with different molecular weight PEGs can lead to different pharmacokinetic properties of ORI conjugates.
we have successfully developed PEG-SA-ORI as a promising antileukemia drug carrier.
